unit_attributes.scope_text: Applies to an employee of a covered employer for purposes of determining whether the employee is an eligible employee under 29 CFR 825.110.
unit_attributes.choice_text: All three criteria are required: (1) employed by the employer for at least 12 months, AND (2) employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding the commencement of the leave (subject to special hours of service requirements for airline flight crew employees under § 825.801), AND (3) employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite (referencing § 825.105(b) for employees working outside the U.S.).
unit_attributes.statement: An eligible employee is an employee of a covered employer who meets all three conditions: has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months; has been employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding the commencement of the leave (noting § 825.801 for airline flight crew employees); and is employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite (noting § 825.105(b) regarding employees working outside the U.S.).

unit_attributes.scope_text: Applies when determining whether an employee has met the requirement to have been employed by the employer for at least 12 months.
unit_attributes.statement: The 12 months an employee must have been employed by the employer need not be consecutive months, provided that the governing rules in 29 CFR 825.110(b) are met.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, subject to the exceptions provided in paragraph (b)(2).
unit_attributes.statement: Subject to the exceptions provided in paragraph (b)(2) of this section, employment periods prior to a break in service of seven years or more need not be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, where an employee has had a break in service of more than seven years and either the break was occasioned by USERRA-covered service or a qualifying written agreement to rehire exists.
unit_attributes.choice_text: Either (i) the break in service is occasioned by fulfillment of a USERRA-covered service obligation, OR (ii) a written agreement, including a collective bargaining agreement, exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service.
unit_attributes.statement: Employment periods preceding a break in service of more than seven years must be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months where: (i) the break in service is occasioned by the fulfillment of the employee's USERRA-covered service obligation, in which case the period of absence due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service must also be counted (without providing any greater entitlement than available under USERRA); or (ii) a written agreement, including a collective bargaining agreement, exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service (such as for education or childrearing purposes).

unit_attributes.scope_text: When determining weeks of employment and whether employment qualifies as at least 12 months.
unit_attributes.statement: If an employee is maintained on the payroll for any part of a week, including any periods of paid or unpaid leave during which other benefits or compensation are provided by the employer (e.g., workers' compensation or group health plan benefits), the week counts as a week of employment; for purposes of determining whether intermittent, occasional, or casual employment qualifies as at least 12 months, 52 weeks is deemed to equal 12 months.

unit_attributes.scope_text: When determining whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement following a continuous break in service of more than seven years.
unit_attributes.statement: Nothing in this section prevents employers from considering employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years when determining whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement.

unit_attributes.scope_text: If an employer chooses to recognize employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years when determining whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement.
unit_attributes.statement: If an employer chooses to recognize employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years, the employer must do so uniformly, with respect to all employees with similar breaks in service.
